security_audit.summary: No malicious behavior or prompt-injection instructions were found in SKILL.md. The static alerts are Markdown formatting, documentation examples, official RunComfy links, expected token storage notes, and RunComfy identity checks. Users should still handle tokens, prompts, media URLs, and downloaded outputs according to the documented privacy guidance.

content.user_title: Automate RunComfy Model Jobs from the CLI
content.value_statement: Creative teams need repeatable access to RunComfy models without switching between tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through setup, authentication, model runs, polling, and downloads.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install the RunComfy CLI with npm or npx.
Guides device-code login and RUNCOMFY_TOKEN authentication.
Shows how to run RunComfy model endpoints with inline or file inputs.
Covers polling, no-wait jobs, status checks, retries, and exit codes.
Describes output download options and JSON output for scripts.
Lists safety notes for tokens, downloads, and trusted endpoints.
limitations: Requires the separate runcomfy CLI to be installed before use.
Requires a RunComfy account and valid token for authenticated model calls.
Can send prompts, media URLs, and generated outputs through RunComfy services.
Does not validate model-specific input schemas beyond CLI guidance.

use_cases.title: Automate Creative Model Calls
use_cases.description: Run image, video, edit, and upscaling jobs from repeatable terminal workflows.

use_cases.title: Create Reproducible Design Outputs
use_cases.description: Submit prompts with consistent inputs and save generated files into named project folders.

use_cases.title: Manage Long Running Jobs
use_cases.description: Submit no-wait requests, store request identifiers, and poll results later from scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RunComfy CLI skill to confirm whether runcomfy is installed and whether I am signed in.

prompt_templates.title: Generate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RunComfy to run a text-to-image model with this prompt: [describe the image]. Save outputs to a project folder.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Prompts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a RunComfy workflow for a prompt list, with one output folder per prompt and clear retry handling.

prompt_templates.title: Automate No-Wait Jobs
prompt_templates.prompt: Submit several RunComfy jobs without waiting, save request identifiers, and show how to poll them later from the CLI.

output_examples.input: Generate a product concept image and save the final file in the project folder.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a suitable text-to-image endpoint, submits the prompt, monitors progress, and reports the downloaded file location.

output_examples.input: Run three video prompts overnight and check results tomorrow.
output_examples.output: The assistant plans no-wait submissions, captures request identifiers, and gives a status-check workflow for the next session.
The assistant explains the likely exit code, checks authentication or input schema issues, and suggests retries only for transient failures.

best_practices: Review any installer before using shell-pipe installation methods.
Store tokens in the CLI token file or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN, and never paste tokens into prompts.
Use JSON output and no-wait mode for scripts that need reliable automation.
anti_patterns: Do not send private media URLs to RunComfy unless the user explicitly approved the upload.
Do not copy model output URLs into public logs without checking sensitivity.
Do not retry validation errors; fix the input schema first.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It teaches agents how to use the runcomfy CLI for RunComfy model jobs, authentication, polling, and downloads.

faq.question: Does it install RunComfy automatically?
faq.answer: It explains supported install paths. The skill itself is scoped to runcomfy commands after installation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. A RunComfy account and a valid CLI token are required for authenticated model calls.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The CLI downloads outputs to the current directory by default, or to a chosen output directory.

faq.question: What data can leave my machine?
faq.answer: Prompts, input files or URLs, and job requests can be sent to RunComfy services during model execution.
